autoLabPersistence.paper: AutoLab — long-horizon agents (persistence under wall-clock budget)

source.title: AutoLab: Can Frontier Models Solve Long-Horizon Auto Research and Engineering Tasks?
source.leaderboardNote: The paper abstract reports 17 evaluated models across 36 tasks. Public-site copy is inconsistent: metadata says 7+ models across 23 tasks, while FAQ text says 11+ models. Treat Claude Opus 4.6 as the clearest strong signal and verify the live leaderboard before making model-selection claims.

autoLabPersistence.appliesTo: Codex, Cursor, and any agent; every ticket that improves a working artifact (backtest accuracy, Brier/calibration, deploy smoke resilience, risk-unit coverage, API latency, UX)
autoLabPersistence.scope: AGENTS.md -> AutoLab Persistence Loop is the governing rule for this repo
autoLabPersistence.summary: Long-horizon task success is predicted by persistence on the benchmark-edit-feedback loop, not first-attempt quality. The paper reports 17 evaluated models across 36 tasks; public-site copy is inconsistent between 7+ and 11+ model signals across 23 tasks. Claude Opus 4.6 is the strongest observed model for sustained long-horizon optimization, while most others either quit early or burn the budget with little measured progress.
loop: start from a green baseline gate; never trade correctness for a metric
define the benchmark first using verificationCommands or a metric API (Brier, calibration, latency, deploy smoke pass-rate); record the baseline measurement
iterate measure -> edit -> re-measure -> fold the result into the next edit
set an explicit budget (iterations or wall-clock) and persist to it; do not hand off after one attempt
track best-so-far; after K consecutive no-progress iterations (default 3) stop and reorganize or retire the direction
keep the best measured artifact; never hand off worse than baseline
autoLabPersistence.benchmarks: verificationCommands above, plus Brier/calibration and deploy smoke-test pass-rate for the relevant gate
guardrails: never weaken PAPER_TRADING_ONLY, the RiskService -> OrderIntent -> OrderBookService order path, or any deploy gate to hit a metric
a benchmark win that regresses a gate or guardrail is a dead end, not progress
autoLabPersistence.handoffLine: AutoLab: baseline=<verified gate/measure> | benchmark=<metric/command> | iterations=<n + best result> | budget=<used/limit> | outcome=<improved / stalled-reorganized / retired>
autoLabPersistence.notApplicable: for a one-shot fix with no measurable axis, record 'AutoLab: not applicable (no iterative measure)'
